title: MHZ Ship Builder - paint styles pack
description: Schema for data/paint_styles.json (API_CONTRACT_SPORE.md sections 10 and 11). Three sibling blocks, one per paint method the vehicle/ship editor offers: 'complete' styles carry one ordered colour per paint region plus a single texture and leave no region untouched; 'partial' styles name only the regions they care about and leave the rest as the player left them; 'textures' is the shared finish vocabulary both style blocks reference by id, and the only place a texture id is defined. Every colour is an INDEX into the 16-entry active palette from data/palette.json, never a hex value, so a budget alert that swaps the whole LUT recolours every painted ship with it. THREE RULES THIS SCHEMA CANNOT EXPRESS, all enforced elsewhere: (1) a 'texture' id must resolve to a key in the 'textures' block - a standalone JSON Schema cannot cross-reference a sibling object; (2) a region id named by a partial style must exist in the target family's 'paint_regions' (data/shapes/families.json) - ShipPaint.plan_partial_style skips any that does not, rather than inventing the region; (3) a complete style's 'colors' array should carry one entry per paint region, which is family-dependent - ShipPaint repeats the last colour when the array is short and drops the extras when it is long. Enforced by tools/ship_validate_data.gd.

_description.description: Must explain what the three blocks are for, that colours are palette INDICES rather than hex values, and what the reserved palette slots mean.

complete.description: Whole-part liveries, keyed by snake_case style id. Applying one leaves NO paint region untouched.

partial.description: Trim and accent packs, keyed by snake_case style id. Applying one touches only the regions it names, so it layers over a complete style instead of replacing it.

textures.description: The shared finish vocabulary, keyed by snake_case texture id. This block is the ONLY place a texture id is defined; both style blocks and ShipPart.paint reference these keys.

lut_index.description: An index into the 16-entry active palette (data/palette.json). Never a hex colour - the indirection is what lets ShipTheme swap the whole LUT for a budget alert and recolour every painted ship with it. AUTHOR THESE AS BARE INTEGERS: JSON Schema 2020-12 accepts 4.0 as an integer and no keyword can refuse it, but Godot's parser reads 4.0 as a float and ShipCanonical emits "4.000000" for a float against "4" for an int, so a hand-edited 4.0 would hash differently from the same ship painted in the editor. ShipPaint rounds such a value back to an int on read; the schema cannot stop it being written.

label.description: Short player-facing name, shown in the paint panel's style and texture lists.

description.description: Real catalogue copy written for a human reader (AGENTS.md section 10b: data/ is documentation). Placeholder strings like 'TODO' fail minLength and are additionally rejected by tools/ship_validate_data.gd's banned-phrase check.

texture_id.description: A key in the 'textures' block. Required, so a complete style always states its finish.

texture_ref.description: A key in the 'textures' block, or the empty string. Inside a PARTIAL style the empty string means 'no texture change' and the part keeps whatever finish it already carries - see teal_wash, which states that in its own prose - so a two-region tint cannot silently strip the finish it was layered over.

region_paint.description: One region's finish, in the same value shape ShipPart.paint stores per region: {"color": int, "texture": String}. Both keys are required so the shape API_CONTRACT_SPORE.md section 2 pins can never be half-written.

colors.description: One palette index per paint region, IN THE FAMILY'S OWN paint_regions ORDER: colors[0] goes to the first region (conventionally 'base', the keel end), colors[1] to the second, and so on. Order is load-bearing and duplicates are legal - a livery that repeats a colour across two regions is a real design, so uniqueItems is deliberately NOT set.

regions.description: The regions this style touches, keyed by region id from a family's 'paint_regions' (data/shapes/families.json). A region the target family does not declare is skipped at apply time rather than invented; every region NOT named here is left exactly as the player left it, which is what makes a partial style layerable.

texture.description: One finish in the shared vocabulary. Phase 1 stores the id on the part and shows the label; the surface treatment itself is not rendered yet (ShipSceneBuilder still colours parts by palette role), so an entry carries no numeric parameters.
